title: Minimax Regret Saddle Points in Nonsmooth Polyhedral Gaussian Endpoint Games
banked_reason: The delivered kernel leaves the advertised primitive all/coexistence/none classifier open; conditional curved-score implication is not a realized no-index frontier.
gap_reasons: The delivered kernel leaves the advertised primitive all/coexistence/none classifier open; conditional curved-score implication is not a realized no-index frontier.
Neither an explicit rational unbalanced-prior interval certificate nor a two-dimensional impossibility theorem is present in, or derivable from, the frozen primitives.
The tested rational candidate fails because b(pi) <= 1/3 < 3/7 <= v.
proof_attempt_summary: The run established a sound compact asymmetric Gaussian endpoint-game core: unrestricted saddle duality, convergent exchange certificates, and an exact coexistence example. A final scoped construction attempted to realize the no-one-index branch with a rational unbalanced prior and exact global interval/tail/curvature certificates, but its candidate was not least favorable and no replacement or impossibility theorem was obtained. The primitive all/coexistence/none criterion and a realized no-index witness therefore remain open.
tldr: The note solves the unrestricted compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game, constructs face-complete least-favorable priors, proves convergence of primal--dual exchange bounds without a complexity-rate claim, and gives a finite sufficient certificate for the no-one-index branch: exact saddle closure for a finite endpoint prior together with a nonvanishing analytic score and one regular curved score-zero arc implies a unique minimax rule outside every measurable one-index class. The asymmetric triangular example has value \(2/3\) and proves coexistence of one-index and non-one-index optima. The requested fully rational unbalanced curved-score witness remains unresolved: an explicit rational attempt has curved boundary \(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\), but exact inequalities rule it out because \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\). The finite all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index primitive criterion also remains open. Conditional feasible transfer uses reverse deficiency only for its lower bound and a separate joint total-variation premise for its upper bound; it makes no sample-splitting derivation or rate claim.
gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. Yata2025Optimal relies on an antipodal modulus pair. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition. AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes solves ex-ante \(\Gamma\)-MMR and ex-post \(\Gamma\)-PER under its equation-(2.9) constrained prior class and derives uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold conclusions, but does not solve the unrestricted endpoint-state minimax-regret correspondence or exclude arbitrary measurable one-index rules. The corrected-proof Abstract of ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules derives asymptotically optimal discrete-choice rules from a hybrid objective: minimax ambiguity treatment for the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter, combined with average-risk minimization for the point-identified parameter. That objective is orthogonal to the exact unrestricted signed-endpoint minimax-regret saddle studied here, and neither objective implies the other.
fill: The project derives unrestricted saddle duality and face-complete dual representatives, then proves that exact finite-prior saddle closure plus a nonvanishing curved Bayes-score boundary yields uniqueness and the no-one-index category. Convergent exchange bounds locate candidate priors, while outward-rounded interval arithmetic closes the global risk inequalities and the local curvature inequalities. The triangular value-\(2/3\) construction remains the coexistence regression test, and the complete normal-fan trichotomy remains answer-open. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary and makes no statistical frontier or rate claim.
